children: Doha, Qatar: Hamad, Ruwais and Doha ports witnessed an increase in handling of bulk cargo and livestock in August this year compared to the previous month.

In a post on its X platform yesterday, Mwani Qatar stated “Qatar ports handled approximately 120,000 tonnes of bulk cargo in August 2026, marking a 168% increase compared to the previous month. Livestock and vessel calls also rose by approximately 191% and 13%, respectively.”

The three ports handled 49,040 twenty-foot equivalent units (TEU) containers, 30,011 tonnes of general cargo, 119,963 tonnes of bulk cargo, 30 units of RORO, and 5,989 heads of live-stock. Meanwhile the ports received 133 vessels in August 2026.
Qatar ports handled more than 493,000 TEUs and nearly 273,000 tonnes of general cargo during the first half of 2026.

The figures indicate the continuing importance of Hamad, Doha and Al Ruwais port to Qatar’s supply chain and wider economic activity. The ports handled more than 324,000 tonnes of bulk cargo between January and June, alongside almost 25,000 RORO units and more than 112,000 livestock. The ports received 866 vessel calls during the period.

Recently, the Ministry of Transport (MoT) completed automating 11 more maritime transportation affairs’ services. Now electronic and accessible via the MoT’s official website, the 11 fresh e-services cover the transactions related to big vessels and seafarers’ affairs.
This brings the total number of e-services available at the MoT’s website to 21, while the MoT continues its plans for simpler transactions, less time and effort, and better user experience.

From world-class infrastructure to a growing shipping network, flexible operational processes, and massive capacity that adapts to market shifts, Hamad Port, Qatar’s main gateway to world trade, provides integrated logistics solutions that empower your business with greater speed, higher efficiency, and broader access to global markets.

The Centralized Customs Inspection Area (CCIA) at Hamad Port plays a key role in facilitating cargo movement and expediting procedures through a smart operational system that ensures precise inspection and reduced clearance times. This boosts seamless trade flows and enhances supply chain efficiency, further solidifying Qatar as a vital and leading logistics hub on the global trade map.

Situated around 27 km from Hamad Port, the Container Management Station at Jery Musabbeh enhances cargo flow and strengthens logistical capabilities, spanning an area of 88,375 square meters with a capacity exceeding 5,000 TEUs.

The Station offers integrated services including storage, inspection, maintenance, and washing for various types of containers, supporting supply chain efficiency and the broader logistics ecosystem in Qatar.
Meanwhile Ruwais port, Qatar’s northern gateway to trade, plays an increasingly strategic role as a regional commercial hub.

By developing its infrastructure and streamlining cargo operations, the port enhances supply chain resilience and drives commercial exchange, in line with the country’s economic diversification plans and strategic goals.
